stem_text: A body of mass 2kg is initially at rest. It starts moving unidirectionally under the influence of a source of constant power P. Its displacement in 4s is (1)/(3)𝛼^(2)√(𝑃)m . The value of 𝛼 will be ______.

candidate_solve.derivation: Mass m = 2 kg. (1/2)*m*v^2 = P*t => (1/2)*(2)*v^2 = P*t => v = sqrt(P)*t^(1/2). Displacement x(t) = int_0^t sqrt(P)*t'^(1/2) dt' = (2/3)*sqrt(P)*t^(3/2). At t = 4s: t^(3/2) = 4^(3/2) = 8 => x(4) = (2/3)*sqrt(P)*8 = (16/3)*sqrt(P) = (1/3)*(16)*sqrt(P). Comparing with (1/3)*alpha^2*sqrt(P): alpha^2 = 16 => alpha = 4.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Connecting constant power to differential kinematics: (1/2)mv^2 = Pt => v = sqrt(2Pt/m)

representation_translation.evidence: Integrating v(t) = sqrt(P)*t^(1/2) with respect to time to obtain displacement formula

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Integrate to find x(t), evaluate at t=4s, equate to target expression (1/3)alpha^2 sqrt(P) to extract alpha

algebra_computational_load.evidence: Evaluating fractional exponent 4^(3/2) = 8 and solving alpha^2 = 16 => alpha = 4

demand_proposal.rationale: Applying calculus integration to constant power velocity function
